comments.body:
PRE-IMPLEMENTATION TRIAGE OF ITEM 3 (validate_assignee_exists): IT IS A PURE TEST GAP, NOT A
LATENT PRODUCT BUG. The plan says 'if any path returns a bool or an accountId-shaped value, a bug is
filed' — checked at df41edcf25 so the implementer does not have to hold that possibility open.

adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:704 declares '-> str' and has exactly TWO exits:
  * return str(_user_attr(user, "name") or assignee)   <- a DC USERNAME string
  * raise AssigneeNotFoundError(...)                     <- the documented miss
No path returns a bool, and none returns an accountId-shaped value. The docstring already states the
return contract in the same terms the ticket does, including why returning True or an accountId
would corrupt the identity, and why the error type must be AssigneeNotFoundError SPECIFICALLY
(outbound_assignee branches on type(exc).__name__, so any other type — a NotImplementedError in
particular — would silently and permanently downgrade every DC assignee resolution to the
non-authoritative string-match fallback).

SO: the contract is implemented and documented; what is missing is any ASSERTION of it. That is
exactly the ticket's characterisation — 'a real gap wearing a test's clothes' — and it means item 3
needs a test written, and NO bug ticket filed. The implementer should still check the CLOUD side
(adapters/jira/acli.py:541) independently rather than inferring parity from this, since the AC asks
for the return value to be asserted for BOTH backends and Cloud's contract is deliberately
different (accountId, not name).

Note the mutation check for this item has to bite on the RETURN VALUE, not on presence: the existing
vacuous assertion is 'assert hasattr(cls, "validate_assignee_exists")', which the parametrized
presence test in the same file already makes verbatim, so a rewrite that still only proves existence
would reproduce the defect this ticket exists to remove.

comments.body:
ITEM 2 CONFIRMED VERBATIM — plus an IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT the plan does not state, which decides
how the fix has to be shaped. Verified at df41edcf25.

THE VACUITY IS EXACTLY AS DESCRIBED. In test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py,
test_the_structural_guard_fires_on_a_synthetic_unpaginated_caller re-implements the AST walk INLINE
(its own ast.parse, its own isinstance(ast.Call)/isinstance(ast.Attribute) checks, its own
attr == 'search_issues' test, its own maxResults/max_results keyword check) rather than calling the
predicate the real guard uses. Its docstring says 'TEETH for the guard itself. A structural test that
cannot fail is decoration' — and it is decoration: the only way it can fail is if the ast module
itself breaks. The real predicate could regress to 'return []' and this cell stays green while
test_no_search_issues_call_relies_on_the_default_page_size silently stops guarding anything.

THE CONSTRAINT — AND IT IS WHY 'JUST CALL THE HELPER' IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX.
_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default() (same file, ~line 145) takes NO PARAMETERS and hardcodes
its input: 'tree = ast.parse(_TRANSPORT_SRC.read_text())'. So the teeth test CANNOT point at it as
written — there is no seam to feed a synthetic file through. Note also it is a TEST-MODULE helper,
not a src/ helper, so 'the production helper' in the plan means 'the predicate the production guard
consumes', which is this function.

THE SHAPE THAT ACTUALLY GIVES IT TEETH: give the helper an optional source parameter, e.g.

    def _search_issues_calls_taking_the_default(src: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
        tree = ast.parse(src if src is not None else _TRANSPORT_SRC.read_text())

Then the real guard keeps calling it with NO argument (unchanged behaviour, and its own assertion is
untouched), while the teeth test calls it WITH the synthetic unpaginated source. That is what makes
the mutation check in this ticket's AC meaningful: breaking the predicate — e.g. dropping the
'max_results' alternative from the keyword set, or making offenders always empty — must turn the
TEETH test red, which is impossible today.

WHAT NOT TO DO, because both preserve the defect while looking like a fix:
 * Do not add a SECOND standalone predicate for the synthetic case. That reproduces the duplication
   that caused the vacuity, and the two copies can then drift — which is the same defect class as
   sibling ticket bd9e-0740-1b47-47f8 in this very epic.
 * Do not settle for asserting the helper merely RUNS on the synthetic input. The assertion must be
   that it REPORTS the offender, since 'returns a list' is satisfied by 'return []'.

MUTATION-CHECK NOTE: mutate the PREDICATE, not the synthetic fixture. Mutating the fixture only
proves the fixture is unpaginated, which nobody doubts.

The negative controls are what make the second mutation bite — asserting only the positive offender
would have stayed green.

ITEM 3 — validate_assignee_exists RETURN VALUE, both backends. NO BUG FILED: the pre-implementation
triage is confirmed on both sides. DC (transport.py) returns str(_user_attr(user,"name") or
assignee) or raises AssigneeNotFoundError. CLOUD (adapters/jira/acli.py) was checked INDEPENDENTLY
and its contract IS deliberately different as expected: it returns u.get("accountId") from an exact

AssigneeNotFoundError; it additionally raises ValueError when neither issue_key nor project_key is

The DC test now CALLS the member (the old body was `assert hasattr(...)`, verbatim what the

MUTATED: DC `return str(_user_attr(user, "name") or assignee)` -> `return True`;
FAILED: test_validate_assignee_exists_returns_the_dc_username
RED: AssertionError: DC must resolve to the USERNAME that flows on as the identity; got True /
assert True == 'dcuser'
MUTATED: DC same return -> str(_user_attr(user, "accountId") or assignee) (accountId-shaped);
FAILED: test_validate_assignee_exists_returns_the_dc_username
RED: ... got '5b10a2844c20165700ede21g' / assert '5b10a2844c20165700ede21g' == 'dcuser'
MUTATED: Cloud exact-match branch `acct = u.get("accountId")` -> u.get("displayName");
FAILED: test_cloud_validate_assignee_exists_returns_the_account_id_not_the_username
RED: AssertionError: Cloud must resolve to the accountId ...; got 'DC User' /
assert 'DC User' == '5b10a2844c20165700ede21g'

ITEM 4 — the 429 enumerated-mutations sweep. total <= 1 is now total == 1, and the blanket
pytest.raises(Exception) (with its # noqa: B017 and its false "the TYPE is asserted per-member
below" comment) is replaced by pytest.raises(BackendHTTPError) with an assertion of .code == 429 per
member. All ten members pass unchanged, which means every one of them genuinely reaches the client
exactly once — the == 1 form is not merely stricter, it is satisfied.
MUTATED: delete_issue_link raises ValueError PRE-FLIGHT (before _call_logged reaches the client);
run in three configurations to isolate which assertion bites:
  * CONFIG A, the OLD form (raises(Exception) + total <= 1): 1 passed — GREEN, the defect reproduced
  * CONFIG B, count teeth only (raises(Exception) + total == 1): FAILED
    test_every_mutating_transport_member_still_fails_on_the_first_429
    RED: AssertionError: delete_issue_link issued 0 client calls under a 429 — exactly one is the
    contract ... ZERO means the member failed BEFORE reaching the client / assert 0 == 1
  * CONFIG C, as committed: FAILED same test, RED: ValueError: MUTANT D: pre-flight failure, client
    never reached (the type assertion catches it even earlier)
MUTATED: retry.py translation drops the status (int(status) if isinstance(status,int) else 0 -> 0);
FAILED: test_every_mutating_transport_member_still_fails_on_the_first_429
RED: AssertionError: create_issue surfaced HTTP 0, not the 429 the client raised — the translation
lost the status ... / assert 0 == 429 + where 0 = <HTTPError 0: 'HTTP 429'>.code

ITEM 5 — unknown backend. BROADENED, not renamed, so the AC's behavioural mutation applies. The test
now imports select_backend/register/_reset_registry_for_test, registers a throwaway sentinel factory
inside the reset context, asserts select_backend resolves it (positive control, so the miss below is
a real miss and not a selector that raises on everything), then asserts the unknown key raises
BackendRegistryError, that the error is not a KeyError instance, and that its message names BOTH the
missing key and the registered ones.
MUTATED: pointed the negative case at the key that DOES resolve ("known-backend-for-this-test");
FAILED: test_an_unknown_backend_raises_the_registry_error_not_key_error
RED: Failed: DID NOT RAISE BackendRegistryError

GATES. Module sizes (LOC before -> after, hard cap 800, none approached it):
test_jira_dc_transport_heldout.py 241 -> 303; test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py 206 -> 221;
test_transport_port_completeness_heldout.py 464 -> 533; test_dc_rate_limit_retry_heldout.py 340 ->
347. No src/** file was modified in the change; every production mutation above was reverted and
`git status` verified clean after each. Full tests/unit/rebar_reconciler: 1886 passed. ruff check +
format and mypy pass via the pre-commit gate. No isinstance() against a runtime-checkable Protocol
was introduced, so the 3.11-vs-3.12 getattr_static change cannot bite; presence is asserted with
hasattr directly.

compiled_state.description:
# Replace the tests that cannot fail

## Context

A parity audit found several tests in both suites whose assertions cannot fail. Each was verified
by reading the body and the code under test — this list is evidence, not suspicion. They are worse
than missing tests: a missing test is visible in a coverage gap, a vacuous one reports coverage it
does not provide, and each of these carries a docstring promising a contract it never checks.

## The confirmed list

**1. `test_jira_dc_transport_heldout.py` — `test_the_pat_never_appears_in_the_repr_of_the_transport`.
A tautology.** Body: `t = JiraDataCenterTransport(client=object(), project="DC")` then
`assert "pat-xyz" not in repr(t)`. The constructor takes `client`/`project`/`resolved_statuses` and
**never receives a PAT at all**; and the class defines no `__repr__`, so `repr(t)` is
`<...object at 0x...>`. The literal `"pat-xyz"` IS used elsewhere in the same module (`:59`, `:72`,
`:87`, `:98`, `:100`) as the PAT fixture fed to `build_client_from_settings` — but it never reaches
the `JiraDataCenterTransport(...)` this test constructs, which is exactly why the assertion is
vacuous. It would pass unchanged if the transport stored and printed a credential. Its docstring — "a credential that
leaks into logs via repr is a real disclosure path" — describes a real risk that is not tested.

**2. `test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` — `test_the_structural_guard_fires_on_a_synthetic_unpaginated_caller`.**
Docstring claims to be "TEETH for the guard itself", but the body RE-IMPLEMENTS the AST predicate
inline (`:187-195`) instead of calling `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` — the module's
own audit helper, defined at `:145` and used by the real guard at `:172`. (It is a TEST-module
helper, not production code; the guard it backs is itself a test.) The teeth test never touches the
predicate it claims to verify; if that predicate regressed, this stays green. It can only fail if
`ast` itself breaks.

**The obvious fix does not work as-is, and that is part of this item's scope.**
`_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` takes NO arguments and hardcodes
`ast.parse(_TRANSPORT_SRC.read_text())` at `:152` — the LIVE transport file. Simply calling it from
the teeth test would scan the real transport, which is currently clean, so the teeth test would pass
regardless of whether the predicate works — the exact vacuity being fixed, reintroduced. The helper
must first be parameterized — an optional source argument (e.g. `src: str | None = None`) falling
back to `_TRANSPORT_SRC.read_text()` — so the real guard at `:172` keeps calling it with NO argument
and unchanged behaviour, while the teeth test hands it the synthetic unpaginated source and asserts
the predicate REPORTS the offender. Two things that look like fixes but preserve the defect: adding
a SECOND standalone predicate for the synthetic case (that is the duplication-drift class sibling
story bd9e exists to remove), and asserting only that the helper RUNS on the synthetic input, which
`return []` already satisfies.

**3. `test_transport_port_completeness_heldout.py` — `test_validate_assignee_exists_returns_the_dc_username`.**
The name and docstring promise the RETURN-VALUE contract ("returning `True`, or an accountId-shaped
value, corrupts the identity"). The body is `assert hasattr(cls, "validate_assignee_exists")` —
already asserted verbatim by the parametrized presence test in the same file. Zero incremental
coverage, and **nothing anywhere asserts DC's `validate_assignee_exists` returns a username string
rather than a bool.** This one is a real gap wearing a test's clothes.

**4. `test_dc_rate_limit_retry_heldout.py` — the enumerated-mutations sweep. MINE, from this epic's
S2, and the criticism is correct.** It asserts `total <= 1` client calls per member. `total == 0`
satisfies that — so a member that raises BEFORE reaching the client (an `AttributeError`, a
pre-flight `ValueError`) never exercises the 429 branch and still passes. `total == 1` is the
assertion with teeth. The `pytest.raises(Exception)` also carries a comment claiming "the TYPE is
asserted per-member below" when the code below only checks counts; the comment overstates what the
test does.

**5. `test_jira_dc_transport_heldout.py` — `test_an_unknown_backend_raises_the_registry_error_not_key_error`.**
Never calls `select_backend`; asserts only `not issubclass(BackendRegistryError, KeyError)`. Real,
but far narrower than its name — it pins a class relationship, not the raising behaviour.

## Approach

For each: decide whether the CONTRACT the docstring names is worth testing. Where it is (1, 3, 4),
write the test the docstring already promises. Where the vacuity is structural (2), point the test
at the shared audit helper it is supposed to be testing — parameterizing that helper first, since
as written it cannot see the synthetic source. Where the name overreaches the assertion (5), either
broaden the test or
narrow the name — do not leave the two disagreeing.

**Do not simply delete them.** Each names a real property; deleting would lose the intent that the
docstring captured. The intent is the valuable part and it should end up asserted.

## Scope

The five tests above. If the fix to (3) reveals that `validate_assignee_exists` does NOT return a
username on some path, that is a bug ticket, not a silent expectation adjustment.

## Testing

Each rewritten test must be MUTATION-CHECKED against the property it now claims — that is the whole
point of this story, and a rewrite that is merely longer has not improved anything.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the PAT-repr test constructs a transport that ACTUALLY carries a credential and asserts the
      credential's own value is absent from `repr` — mutation-checked by adding a `__repr__` that
      leaks it
- [ ] `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()`
      (`test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py:145`) takes an optional source argument falling back
      to `_TRANSPORT_SRC.read_text()`, leaving the real guard's call at `:172` behaviourally
      unchanged — and there is still exactly ONE such predicate in the module
- [ ] the structural-guard teeth test calls that SHARED predicate with the SYNTHETIC unpaginated
      source instead of re-implementing the AST walk inline, and asserts it REPORTS the offender
      (not merely that it returns a list, which `return []` satisfies). MUTATION: break the
      PREDICATE — not the fixture — e.g. make `offenders` always empty, or drop `"max_results"` from
      the accepted keyword set, and confirm the teeth test goes RED. Mutating the fixture only
      proves the fixture is unpaginated, which nobody doubts
- [ ] `validate_assignee_exists` is asserted to return the USERNAME STRING for both backends, not
      merely to exist; if any path returns a bool or an accountId-shaped value, a bug is filed.
      MUTATION: make the stub return `True` (and separately an accountId-shaped
      `"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g"`) and confirm the assertion goes RED for each
- [ ] the rate-limit sweep asserts `total == 1` per member — NOT `total <= 1`, because `0` satisfies
      `<=` and means the 429 branch was never reached — AND replaces the blanket
      `pytest.raises(Exception)` at `test_dc_rate_limit_retry_heldout.py:138` with the specific
      escaping type, `pytest.raises(BackendHTTPError)`, asserting `.code == 429` per member. The
      `# noqa: B017` and the now-true "the TYPE is asserted per-member below" comment go away with
      it. Correcting the comment WITHOUT asserting the type does NOT satisfy this criterion.
      MUTATION: restore `total <= 1` and make one member raise before it reaches the client (e.g.
      a pre-flight `ValueError`), and confirm the `== 1` form goes RED where `<= 1` stayed green
- [ ] the unknown-backend test either exercises `select_backend` (preferred) or is renamed to what
      it actually pins, so name and assertion agree. MUTATION: if it was broadened, point it at a
      backend name that DOES resolve and confirm it goes RED; if it was renamed instead, record
      that no behavioural mutation applies because the test pins only a class relationship
- [ ] every rewritten test is mutation-checked with the mutation and verdict recorded on this ticket

file_impact.reason: rewrite the tautological PAT-repr test and the unknown-backend test (items 1 and 5)
point the structural-guard teeth test at the production predicate instead of re-implementing it (item 2)
assert validate_assignee_exists returns the DC username string, not merely that it exists (item 3)
tighten the enumerated-mutations sweep from total<=1 to total==1 and assert the escaping exception type (item 4)

compiled_state.title: Replace the tests that cannot fail (both suites)
